structured_output.summary: The pull request makes the HTTP client retry a failed request up to three times with exponential backoff, as its description says. The retry loop is in src/retry.ts and the client wraps every call in it. The delay it computes is never used, so the retries do not back off.

intent.note: Three attempts are made (src/retry.ts:18-27), but the backoff the description promises is computed at :22 and never awaited.

findings.title: The computed delay is never passed to setTimeout
findings.explanation: `delayMs` is computed on line 22, but line 24 awaits `setTimeout(resolve)` with no delay, so every retry fires at once and a rate-limited service sees three requests in the same millisecond.

findings.title: The description promises jitter that the code does not add
findings.explanation: The description says each delay has random jitter; nothing in the retry loop adds any, so clients that fail together retry together.
evidence: src/retry.ts:13-27 — no call to Math.random or any jitter helper

inconclusive.question: Does the upstream service send Retry-After on a 429?
inconclusive.what_would_settle_it: The service's API documentation, which is not in this repository.
